section_summary: This section documents the withdrawal, requisitioning, and diversion of Japanese merchant ships in mid-1941, alongside reports about cargo, passengers, and shipping offices. It also covers Panama Canal transit restrictions, security concerns involving Japanese vessels, and the cancellation of Peruvian cotton bookings. Many pages are cross-reference notes pointing to papers filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Walden letter forwarding shipping memorandum
subfiles.about: Reports a plan to clear Japanese ships from the North Atlantic by July 13.
subfiles.summary: Walden forwards a shipping memorandum and says he will also send it to Naval Intelligence.

subfiles.title: Shipments—Japan
subfiles.about: Details the rapid withdrawal of Japanese shipping from U.S. Atlantic and Gulf ports.
subfiles.summary: Japanese lines have stopped scheduling later sailings and are directing vessels to depart by mid-July. Vaughan lists affected ships, cargoes, routes, and indications of government direction.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walden's letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the shipping memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Walden for his July 3 letter and enclosure.

subfiles.title: Reports of Japanese vessel commandeering
subfiles.about: Relays reports that Japan may commandeer merchant vessels for troop movements.
subfiles.summary: Unconfirmed reports describe roughly 91 vessels being taken around July 25 to move troops toward Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Shanghai telegram 851
subfiles.about: Restates the reported requisition and possible troop transport.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases the Shanghai report of Japanese vessel commandeering.

subfiles.title: Further paraphrase of Shanghai telegram 851
subfiles.about: Circulates the Shanghai requisition report.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes unconfirmed reports of ship commandeering and troop movements.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard transmittal concerning Tokai Maru
subfiles.about: Forwards information about Tokai Maru.
subfiles.summary: Sends the attached vessel report for information and possible action.

subfiles.title: Summary of information concerning Tokai Maru
subfiles.about: Records a disputed lubricant request and earlier camera violations by crew members.
subfiles.summary: Tokai Maru cancelled a Baltimore lubricant purchase after questioning; two officers had been fined for camera use in the Canal Zone.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for enclosure 598

subfiles.summary: Charge form with file and enclosure numbers.

subfiles.title: FBI letter on NYK freight priorities
subfiles.about: Reports that NYK is prioritizing Japanese freight and reducing sailings.
subfiles.summary: A confidential informant says NYK instructed offices to favor Japanese cargo and give American freight secondary attention.

subfiles.title: Request concerning Tatuta Maru passengers and cargo
subfiles.about: Asks that Tatuta Maru dock and discharge passengers and American-owned cargo.
subfiles.summary: The firm urges action to secure discharge of passengers and paid-for imports.

subfiles.title: Japanese steamship service to South America
subfiles.from: Walter V. Donnell, American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Forwards a shipping agent's denial that Japanese service to South America will cease.
subfiles.summary: The agent says Panama Canal access is unnecessary to continue service.

subfiles.title: Osaka Line letter to Correio da Manhã
subfiles.about: Denies plans to suspend Japanese shipping service to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Sato says ships can sail via the Strait of Magellan or Cape Horn and names an expected August arrival.

subfiles.title: English translation of Osaka Line letter
subfiles.about: Translates the assurance that Japan–Brazil shipping can continue without Panama Canal transit.
subfiles.summary: The company proposes Rio de Janeiro as a terminus if southern routing becomes necessary.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo on Japanese steamers at the Panama Canal
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese Ambassador's complaint about Japanese steamers denied Panama Canal transit.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary describes canal repairs and suggests that any transit exceptions may favor U.S. defense cargoes.

subfiles.title: Conversation on detention at Cristóbal
subfiles.about: Records Ambassador Nomura's request for help with Japanese steamers held at Cristóbal.
subfiles.summary: Nomura asks about three detained vessels and six approaching ships. The Acting Secretary cites canal repairs and possible priority for U.S. defense cargoes.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard transmittal of sabotage report
subfiles.about: Forwards a report of alleged sabotage plans against Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Covell sends the enclosed information for possible action.

subfiles.title: Alleged plans to sabotage Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Relays an allegation that Italian agents planned to blow up a Japanese ship at San Pedro.
subfiles.summary: The Coast Guard rates the source reliable but the information undetermined.

subfiles.title: FBI forwarding sabotage allegation
subfiles.about: Forwards the same allegation of a planned attack on a Japanese ship.
subfiles.summary: Hoover says no further information is available and promises to forward developments.

subfiles.title: Requisition of Kongo Maru and Azumasan Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese government control of two ships and disrupted bookings.
subfiles.summary: Kongo Maru was withdrawn from Orient–New York service; Osaka reports both ships requisitioned after cargo had been loaded.

subfiles.title: Request to relay telegram 848 to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Directs transmission of the earlier shipping telegram for information.
subfiles.summary: Refers to telegram 848 of June 19.

subfiles.title: Military Intelligence transmittal
subfiles.about: Forwards a Panama Canal Department report on Japanese shipping.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the July 22 weekly shipping report.

subfiles.title: Weekly report on Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: Accounts for Japanese vessels at the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Six ships departed Cristóbal for Rio without transiting; eight earlier northbound vessels remained unaccounted for locally.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese vessel departure
subfiles.about: Points to a report about a Japanese vessel leaving Canadian waters without loading licensed wheat.
subfiles.summary: Original paper filed at 201.429.1/21.

subfiles.title: Return of papers to Tenney
subfiles.about: Returns papers discussed earlier.
subfiles.summary: Salmon returns papers Tenney had left with him.

subfiles.title: Shanghai confirmation of telegram delivery
subfiles.about: Confirms delivery of the June 19 telegram about vessel requisitioning.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai's naval radio station records delivery to the Department on June 20.

subfiles.title: NYK commercial sailings to cease
subfiles.about: Reports a confidential prediction that NYK will stop foreign commercial sailings.
subfiles.summary: Source says no NYK ship will sail abroad commercially after Asama Maru departs on August 28.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase for Naval Operations
subfiles.about: Relays the Kobe report on NYK sailings.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases the predicted suspension after Asama Maru's sailing.

subfiles.title: Cancellation of Peruvian cotton bookings
subfiles.about: Reports cancellation of cotton space on four Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Agents cite Japanese cotton controls; exporters suspect the U.S. freeze on Japanese funds and expect shipments once payment is arranged.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Lima cotton telegram
subfiles.about: Circulates the Lima report on cancelled cotton bookings.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the reported cancellations, official explanation, and exporters' view of the funds embargo.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Rakuyo Maru fuel oil
subfiles.about: Points to instructions refusing bunkering applications pending ministry approval.
subfiles.summary: Original paper filed at 840.51 Frozen Credits/2952.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Kiyokawa Maru detention
subfiles.about: Points to the Ecuadorian detention of Kiyokawa Maru on suspicion of arms loading.
subfiles.summary: Original paper filed at 722.2315/1802.

subfiles.title: FBI report on NYK office closures
subfiles.about: Reports that NYK offices in the United States are closing.
subfiles.summary: Hoover says Chicago, New York, Los Angeles, and San Francisco offices received closure notices and no further passenger ships would dock.

subfiles.title: Japanese cancellation of cotton shipments
subfiles.about: Analyzes the cancellation of Peruvian cotton bookings.
subfiles.summary: Exporters connect cancellations to the freeze on Japanese funds and difficulty securing dollar payment. One believes ships remain available and expects most contracted cotton to ship.

subfiles.title: NYK circular cancelling Peruvian cotton bookings
subfiles.about: Cancels bookings on Akagi, Heiyo, Sanuki, and Awata Maru.
subfiles.summary: Agents say a Japanese Cotton Control Committee will allocate future space directly.

subfiles.title: Walden report from Batavia
subfiles.about: Reports the departure of a Japanese delegation from Batavia.
subfiles.summary: Walden quotes his Dutch manager's telegram that the delegation left for Japan.

subfiles.title: Embassy archives aboard Norfolk Maru
subfiles.from: Langdon, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Records inquiry about suspected canal sabotage and sealed Japanese Embassy archives.
subfiles.summary: Military Intelligence asked whether 22 archive cases aboard Norfolk Maru could be opened. Far Eastern Affairs opposed this, and Crane told Bratton the Embassy seals were inviolate.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Norfolk Maru delay
subfiles.about: Explains Customs inspection of Norfolk Maru following a sabotage allegation.
subfiles.summary: Customs searched the vessel and inspected its exterior for explosives. The note proposes telling the Japanese Embassy that departure should not be unduly delayed.

subfiles.title: Okumura inquiry about Norfolk Maru
subfiles.about: Records the Japanese Embassy's concern about Norfolk Maru and its archive cases.
subfiles.summary: Okumura asks why the ship has been held at Baltimore. Schuler promises to investigate and reply.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning Tatuta Maru and George Carver
subfiles.about: Records an inquiry about a missionary reportedly detained aboard Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.summary: Officials suggest local legal inquiry, then learn Tatuta Maru has not entered San Francisco and may have turned back into the Pacific.

subfiles.title: File charge record
subfiles.about: Records a charge involving another numbered file.
subfiles.summary: Administrative form with fragmentary handwritten entries.

subfiles.title: Confidential conversation on detention at Cristóbal
subfiles.about: Records Nomura's complaint about Japanese steamers denied Panama Canal transit.
subfiles.summary: A clearer copy of the conversation at pages 120–121: Welles offers to investigate and discusses canal repairs and priority for U.S. defense cargoes.

subfiles.title: Welles letter enclosing Cristóbal memorandum
subfiles.about: Sends the Nomura conversation memorandum to the Ambassador in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the July 18 memorandum in strict confidence.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese vessels remaining at sea
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on ships avoiding U.S. ports amid detention rumors.
subfiles.summary: Original paper filed at 711.94/2213.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Guayaquil and Kiyokawa Maru
subfiles.about: Points to reporting on anti-Japanese demonstrations and detention of Kiyokawa Maru.
subfiles.summary: Original paper filed at 722.2315/1903.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese ships off Callao
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese ships off Callao, obscured flags, and uncertainty over oil policy.
subfiles.summary: The fragment says Japanese ships were ordered to avoid U.S. ports and asks about oil supply policy.

subfiles.title: Request for information on diverted Japanese ships
subfiles.about: Seeks details of Japanese ships diverted from U.S. ports and their legal status.
subfiles.summary: The firm requests a list of requisitioned vessels and asks how other ships were prevented from completing voyages.
